name: Domain Atlas — Spatial Web Reader
description: Detects a domain's spatial manifest (/.well-known/spatial.json) and lets you step into the worlds it declares, within a domain or across domains, carrying a real signed-credential wallet — items, loadouts with transfer-on-loss, fungible resources, and trading-station settlement — between them. The wallet itself also opens as a real browser side panel from the toolbar button on any page, independent of whether that page declares a manifest at all — docked beside the page rather than drawn over it. A page may also ask the wallet directly, read-only, whether an identity is active and what its public key is, when its own domain's manifest opts it in (SPEC.md §3.8), ask it to sign an application-defined payload for a manifest-whitelisted purpose (SPEC.md §3.8.1), or offer it a complete, already-signed asset credential for a manifest-whitelisted asset class — which never lands straight in the wallet, only in a sandboxed pending-offers tray the visitor separately claims or dismisses (SPEC.md §3.8.2), unless the visitor has separately chosen to trust that site for future offers, which skips the prompt and the tray entirely for whatever that site's manifest already has whitelisted (SPEC.md §3.8.3) — each confirmed, when required, through a prompt the page cannot see into or control. A page may also ask the wallet to show a preview of an asset it holds, in a panel the extension draws (SPEC.md §3.8.5).
